query_text: Need a collaborative online whiteboard tool that the teacher and all students can draw and write on at the same time during class, where everyone can see each other's changes live in the browser without any delay, and the teacher can also lock certain areas so only they can write there while students work on their own sections, all accessible from a regular desktop web browser with no software to install.

Create a website that tells the hundred-year story of a brand in a way that actually feels worth looking at, with a richly layered timeline running along the side where each decade has its own mood and color palette, and clicking into any era brings up the old logos, packaging, and ad imagery from that period in a way that feels more like flipping through a beautifully printed book than scrolling a webpage, all designed for a desktop browser so the wide layout really breathes.

Need a magazine cover archive gallery app that lets you browse decades of covers in a visually lush way right in the desktop browser, where the covers are displayed large enough to actually appreciate the typography and photography of each era, and you can filter by decade or publication so the whole thing feels like wandering through a curated art collection rather than a plain image search.

Create a website for browsing historical newspaper front pages, where the overall feel is warm and slightly aged like old newsprint but still clean and easy to read on a desktop browser, with a timeline you can scrub through by year or decade to pull up front pages from that moment in history, and each page should show a nicely rendered image of the full front page alongside a short note about the headline story.

Create a book catalog showcase app for a publishing house where the whole thing feels like stepping into a well-designed independent bookshop, displayed beautifully in a desktop browser with covers shown large and the sidebar letting you filter by genre or year, and clicking any title opens a clean spread with the cover art front and center, a short description, and a list of related titles from the same series or author.

Build a literary journal back-issue archive browser that has the kind of quiet, considered visual quality you'd expect from the journals themselves, running in a desktop browser where the layout gives each issue its own cover image and a gentle year label, and browsing feels like pulling volumes off a shelf, with the ability to click into any issue and read the table of contents with contributor names listed in elegant type.

Need a podcast network directory app that works in a desktop browser and feels visually rich rather than flat and utilitarian, where each show has its own cover art displayed prominently and a sidebar lets you browse by topic or host, and clicking a show takes you to its episode list with the key art staying visible so the whole experience feels more like browsing a record store than a plain list of links.

Make a documentary film series showcase app for desktop browsers where each film in the series gets its own full-width still image as the backdrop, with the synopsis laid over it in clean readable type, and a filmstrip-style row at the top lets you move between titles in the series so the pacing feels slow and cinematic rather than rushed, with the stills chosen for mood so the whole app feels like a carefully curated film program.

Build a heritage site app for a news brand that celebrates its history of design and typography, running in a desktop browser with a layout that itself references the brand's visual legacy, where you can explore how the masthead and typefaces evolved over the decades through large specimen images and short written context, and the overall tone is reverent and editorial, like a retrospective exhibition catalog brought to the web.

A bestseller list retrospective timeline app for desktop browsers where each year on the timeline glows with the aesthetic of that moment, cover art from the top titles of each year arranged in a row so you can feel the shift in publishing tastes across decades, and hovering on any title brings up a small panel with the author, a one-line description, and how many weeks it held the top spot, all rendered with warm typography that makes the whole thing feel like a love letter to reading culture.

Need a wire service archive photography showcase app that treats these historical press photos with the same visual respect you'd give fine art, running in a desktop browser with a generous layout where the images fill most of the screen and the caption and dateline appear in clean secondary type alongside, and a filter along the top lets you narrow by decade or subject so browsing feels like curating a photography book rather than searching a database.

A newsroom staff and correspondent profile directory app, beautifully laid out in a desktop browser where each journalist gets a portrait and a short bio written in a warm, human tone rather than a dry resume format, with the left side letting you filter by beat or region and the profiles themselves arranged in a grid that feels considered and editorial, the kind of page where you actually want to linger and read rather than scan and leave.

Need a website that turns a company annual report into something visually stunning and actually worth exploring in a desktop browser, where the numbers and milestones from the year are presented through large illustrated charts and bold typographic callouts that feel more like a magazine spread than a financial document, and you can click into any section to get more detail while the overall layout stays clean and editorial throughout.

Make a data journalism visual explainer archive app that collects all the past illustrated explainers and data stories in one place for desktop browsers, with each piece shown as a preview image and a short headline so browsing the collection feels like flipping through a coffee table book of visual storytelling, and clicking any piece opens it full width with the original charts and illustrations intact so nothing gets cramped or loses its intended visual impact.

Make a feature stories column app for desktop browsers that gives long-form writing the visual presentation it deserves, where each piece opens with a full-width atmospheric photo, the headline is set in large editorial type that sets the right mood before you even start reading, and a sidebar on the left shows the rest of the column's recent pieces with their cover images so the reader can wander between stories the way you'd browse a beautiful print magazine.

Make a podcast show site for desktop browsers that feels warm and inviting rather than technical, where the show's cover art sits large and front and center, the episode list below it has a generous layout with each episode's title and a one-line description shown clearly, and the overall visual tone matches the personality of the show through thoughtful color choices and typography that makes even first-time visitors feel like they already know what this podcast is about.

Build a digital journal app for desktop browsers where each issue feels like a real publication rather than a plain webpage, with the current issue's cover displayed prominently at the top, a clean table of contents where each article entry has a small mood image alongside the title, and past issues accessible through a back-catalog shelf that shows their covers lined up the way physical journals would look on a reading room table.

Create a long-form investigative journalism platform focused on local regions, built as a web app for desktop browsers, where each investigation gets a beautifully designed opening spread with a strong lead photo and a standfirst that draws you in before the full piece begins, and a region filter in the sidebar lets readers browse stories by area so local journalism feels as carefully presented as the best national magazines.

Make a digital photo essay and photojournalism publication app where the whole experience in a desktop browser feels cinematic and slow, each photo essay opening with a single large image that fills most of the screen, the text flowing alongside in measured paragraphs so the writing and photography breathe together, and a front page that shows recent essays through their lead images in a layout that looks handpicked rather than algorithmically generated.

Build a science explainer and research translation newsroom website for desktop browsers that has the visual intelligence of a design-forward magazine, where each explainer piece uses well-chosen illustrations or diagrams displayed at a scale that actually lets you see what they mean, the tone throughout feels approachable and curious rather than academic, and the home layout groups stories by theme in a way that looks genuinely considered rather than just sorted by date.

Create a literary excerpt and book review editorial site as a web app for desktop browsers, where the reading experience itself feels precious and unhurried, with each review opening in a clean wide column of text set in a typeface that makes you want to keep reading, the book cover shown to one side at a generous size, and a section on the home screen that surfaces recent excerpts with pull quotes displayed in a size large enough to stop you mid-scroll.

Create a documentary film companion text and transcript archive app for desktop browsers, where each film's companion materials are organized in a calm, well-spaced layout that lets the writing stand on its own, with the film's key still images woven into the text at natural intervals rather than shoved into a gallery, and a sidebar index showing all the films in the archive so you can move between companion pieces the way you'd browse a well-organized library collection.

Build a data-driven journalism and interactive chart newsroom app for desktop browsers where the charts and visual stories are treated as the main event rather than decoration, each piece opening with its most striking chart displayed large so the insight hits you immediately, the surrounding text minimal and purposeful, and a home layout that previews the visual character of each story through a thumbnail of its lead chart so the whole site feels like a gallery of illuminating ideas.

Make a opinion and editorial commentary magazine site for desktop browsers that has the confident visual voice of a publication that knows exactly what it stands for, with each piece introduced by a bold typographic treatment of the headline that sets a tone before a word of the article is read, contributor portraits shown with a warmth that makes the writers feel like real people, and a home layout that groups pieces by conversation thread so related opinions and responses are shown together.

Create a web app for desktop browsers where readers can browse and annotate academic preprints in a digest format that actually feels pleasant to spend time in, with each preprint entry showing a short plain-language summary alongside the original title so you can decide whether to go deeper, and a personal notes area on the right side of the reading view where your annotations sit visibly alongside the text in a calm, typographically refined layout that makes serious reading feel less overwhelming.
